neighbours.label: function words in text written for young children (simple explanations, questions to the reader)
fire: Bees are busy bugs that make honey! Can you buzz like a bee?
When you get a cold, your nose gets runny and you might need a tissue.
Look out the window. What color is the sky today?
A caterpillar eats and eats until it is ready to turn into a butterfly.
Firefighters are the people that help put out fires in our town!
What do you see in the picture? Point to the big red truck.
Your heart is a muscle that pumps blood all around your body.
Some animals sleep all winter long. Do you know what that is called?
quiet: Honeybees are eusocial insects that produce honey from floral nectar.
Upper respiratory infections commonly cause rhinorrhea and nasal congestion.
Atmospheric scattering of sunlight determines the apparent color of the sky.
Lepidopteran larvae undergo metamorphosis within a pupal case.
Municipal fire departments respond to structural fires and emergencies.
The photograph depicts a red fire engine parked outside a station.
The cardiac muscle pumps blood through the systemic circulation.
Several mammal species hibernate during the winter months.
